notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Three new ports in Ports and Apps, each made from your own copy of the game.

Call of Duty: Black Ops Zombies, the 2011 phone game, now runs natively at up to 60 fps,
built on r4lix's codboz-nx with the author's permission. It needs your Android copy of the
game, version 1.0.11 (its .apk): on the web page, open Ports and Apps, Call of Duty: Black
Ops Zombies, Files, and add it to Game files. The first start makes the game from it and
downloads the game's texture pack from Activision's server (488 MB, once), so the console
needs the internet then. Play Online uses the community server the game's other ports
share. The menus take touch: tap the screen, or docked press Capture for a mouse on the
right stick and click with R3. Hold Minus for two seconds for the port's settings.

Mario Kart 64 (SpaghettiKart) plays from your US cartridge ROM in your N64 library, beside
Ship of Harkinian and 2 Ship 2 Harkinian. The first start prepares the game from the ROM.
It runs at 30 fps; 60 is an option in Performance settings. Its mods go on the web page
with the two Zeldas'.

Space Cadet Pinball plays the table from your own Windows XP Pinball or Full Tilt! Pinball
files, with its music and sounds, at 60 fps. Add them to its Game files on the web page;
the whole folder is fine. A launches the ball, L and R are the flippers, the D-pad nudges
the table, X starts a new game and Plus pauses; the pre-launch menu remaps them.

Wind Waker HD: docked on a TV it now draws at 1080p (handheld stays at 720p), with the
resolution for each mode in its Graphics tab, whose choices are now saved. Its settings
menu takes A and B by their labels, and Prepare graphics in the Graphics tab visits every
place to build the game's shaders ahead of time, as on the Switch. Each rumble stop is now
sent again, for the rumble that stayed on. On the web page, Rebuild now gets the update
(about 35 minutes, plugged in).

The right-stick mouse's R3 click now lasts as long as a real click, so games that missed
the old instant one see it.

Black Ops Zombies was tested handheld on one console; docked on a TV and an online match
were not tried. Mario Kart 64 was not raced with a controller or tried docked. Pinball can
miss a button pressed in its first few seconds. The Wind Waker HD update was tested on one
console outside the launcher; 1080p on a real TV was not tried, and the rumble never stayed
on in testing, so that fix is untested.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
